notes: Plan-only evals. A pipeline run would dispatch real background from-issue --auto agents (hours of wall clock, background-task notifications the sandbox cannot observe), so these grade the dispatcher discipline instead. This skill lives in the Claude-only tree (home/common/claude-code/skills/); run-eval.sh reaches it through its second skill root. Expected outputs assert role boundaries and the durable-ledger lifecycle, not prose.

evals.name: dispatcher-role-and-ledger-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Orchestrate issues 12, 14 and 15 on this repo. **Plan-only: dispatch nothing, run nothing.** Describe exactly what you would do from invocation to the first agent spawn, then how you'd wait. Be explicit about: what you personally will and will not read; every query you'd run before the first dispatch and how many of each; and what each dispatch prompt contains.
evals.expected_output: Role first: the dispatcher holds a ledger of issue -> state and never reads code, specs, plans, diffs, or review content — context stays flat regardless of issue count. Pre-dispatch: resolve the issue set in the given order; resolve maxParallel (default 2) through `~/.agents/bin/resolve-bindings`, which `orchestration.maxParallel` in .claude/skills.config.json overrides; ONE query for blocked_by edges (dispatch only unblocked issues, re-check the frontier as issues complete — never serialize by reading code); ONE fog pre-check query listing open wayfinder:* decision tickets, intersected with the blocked_by numbers — an issue blocked by an open decision ticket is recorded `fogged` with the links, and nothing is dispatched for it. Lifecycle: choose a stable run_id, resolve the dispatcher's absolute repo root once, run workflow-state init-run then reconcile, and rebuild the local ledger from the durable one; per issue, reserve a collision-free absolute worktree path (verified absent from filesystem AND `git worktree list` — reservation does not create it), call workflow-state launch, and spawn only when the returned attempt is active. Each dispatch is a background general-purpose agent carrying ONLY the lifecycle envelope (ledger_repo_root, run_id, attempt, owner, worktree) plus the literal from-issue <num> --auto invocation — never inlined issue bodies, specs, or plans; the child fetches its own issue. Waiting is event-driven: background agents notify on exit; no sleep loops, no polling, no no-op commands; reconcile on resume/notification/before-retry/before-drain, durable result beats notification text, and the next queued issue dispatches only after reconciliation frees a slot. Failures: reading issue content to order the set, spawning before launch confirms an active attempt, polling in a loop, or holding spec/diff content in the dispatcher.

evals.name: failure-policy-verdicts-vs-retries
evals.prompt: Mid-orchestration status check, plan-only — tell me exactly what you'd do next for each of these, and which ones get a retry: (a) the agent on issue 12 has been silent for two hours; (b) issue 14's agent came back reporting it stopped at from-issue's fog gate; (c) issue 15's agent died when the harness crashed; (d) issue 15's second attempt also died the same way.
evals.expected_output: (a) Silence past the attempt budget — the wall-clock allowance for one attempt, resolved as agentBudgetMinutes through `~/.agents/bin/resolve-bindings` (default 90 min, orchestration.agentBudgetMinutes overrides) — is handled through workflow-state reconcile, which persists a provisional `stopped` outcome that RETAINS the worktree and carries result_source "expiry", so a later finish from that attempt's own owner can still replace it; it is surfaced for human inspection, not auto-relaunched — the failure policy is applied first and any relaunch goes back through workflow-state launch. (b) A fog-gate stop is a content-level VERDICT, not an error: record the child's stated reason verbatim in the ledger, never retry in this run; fogged clears only when the blocking decision tickets close. (c) A harness death is a transient failure: reconcile first — if the durable outcome still permits a retry, workflow-state launch issues a fresh owner identity (attempt 2) — the owner handle, not the workspace, decides fresh-vs-resume — and its --worktree is the prior attempt's recorded worktree whenever one `git worktree list --porcelain` scan shows that exact path still checked out on this issue's branch, else a freshly reserved collision-free path; the spawn happens only from its accepted result. (d) The helper allows attempts 1 and 2 only and refuses a third — record the durable failed outcome; no prose-counted third try. Throughout: a failed issue never blocks unrelated issues, and every state change flows through the durable ledger rather than the dispatcher's memory. Failures: retrying the fog verdict, relaunching the silent agent without reconcile + launch, a third attempt, or discarding the stopped agent's worktree.
